'''Anton Walter Freud''' (3 April 1921 – 8 February 2004) was a [[chemical engineer]] and a member of the [[Royal Pioneer Corps]] and the British [[Special Operations Executive]]. He was a grandson of [[Sigmund Freud]] and escaped with him and other family members from [[Vienna]] after the [[Anschluss]].

== Life ==
Freud was born in Vienna in 1921. He was the first child of Sigmund Freud’s eldest son Jean-Martin (Martin), a lawyer, and his wife Ernestine Drucker. He was named after Anton von Freund, a colleague of his grandfather.

After leaving Vienna in March 1938,<ref>{{Cite web|last=van der Vat|first=Dan|date=9 March 2004|title=Walter Freud obituary|url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2004/mar/09/guardianobituaries.military1|website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> Freud's parents separated, and he and his father went to Britain whilst his mother and sister [[Sophie Freud|Sophie]] went to [[Paris]] before emigrating to the USA.<ref>{{cite book |title=Living in the shadow of the Freud family |first1=Sophie |last1=Freud |first2=Ernestine Drucker|last2=Freud |pages=434–435}}</ref> While he was a student at [[Loughborough College]], he and his father were [[interned]] as enemy aliens in May 1940.  He was first held in a prison in [[Leicester]] and then on the [[Isle of Man]]. In July, he was deported to [[Australia]] aboard the {{Ship|HMT|Dunera}}.

He was allowed to return to the United Kingdom in October 1941 due to a refinement in internment policy.  He then joined the [[Royal Pioneer Corps]] in which he worked for eighteen months, before he was allowed to join the [[Special Operations Executive]] in 1943, due in part to his being a native German speaker. In April 1945 he parachuted into [[Styria]] in the [[Austrian Alps]] to help establish a British presence in advance of the approaching [[Red Army]]. Though he became separated from his comrades, he managed to bluff his way into the strategically important Zeltweg airfield. Posing as a representative of the advancing [[Eighth Army (United Kingdom)|British Eighth Army]], he convinced the Commandant to surrender it to the Allied forces.<ref>Fry, Helen (2009). ''Freuds' War''. Stroud: The History Press,  pp. 161-65</ref>

After the war ended, Freud was posted to the War Crimes Investigation Unit. He was the first person to interrogate [[Bruno Tesch]], head of [[Tesch & Stabenow]], the firm responsible for supplying much of the [[Zyklon B]] gas used in [[Nazi extermination camps]], which led to his trial and execution for war crimes. He was also involved in the investigation of [[Alfried Krupp]] of [[ThyssenKrupp|Krupp Industries]], subsequently indicted for the use of slave labor, and in  the investigation of the murder of twenty Jewish children, the subject of medical experimentation by the Nazi doctor [[Kurt Heissmeyer]], in the basement of the [[Bullenhuser Damm]] school in [[Hamburg]]. In January 1946 he was sent to Denmark to track down and investigate a suspected Nazi war criminal, Gustav Jepsen, subsequently tried and hanged for his crimes. It was in [[Copenhagen]] that he met his future wife, Annette Krarup, a Danish civil servant.  They married in August 1947, Freud having  left active service with the rank of Major in September 1946.<ref>Fry, Helen (2009). ''Freuds' War''. Stroud: The History Press,  pp. 177-83</ref>

After naturalising as a British subject in January 1947,<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=37908 |date=18 March 1947 |page=1264 |supp=y }}</ref> Freud returned to Loughborough, where he graduated with a degree in [[chemical engineering]]. He was hired by [[The BOC Group|British Oxygen Corporation]], then went to work for [[British Nylon Spinners]] in [[Pontypool]]. He was recruited by British Hydrocarbons based in [[London]] in 1957, which after a series of mergers became part of BP Chemicals, where he remained until his retirement at the age of 55 in 1977.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/1453935/Walter-Freud.html|title=Walter Freud|date=11 February 2004 }}</ref>

In 1994 he returned to Vienna for the first time since his enforced exile as a guest of the Austrian government, which marked his achievement in liberating the Zeltweg airfield by hosting a dinner in his honour.<ref>Freud, David (2006) ''Freud in the City'', London: BFP, p. 177</ref> His last residence in Britain was in [[Oxted]], [[Surrey]].<ref>{{cite news|date=25 February 2004|title=Obituary: Walter Freud|page=34|work=[[The Times]]|issue=68007|url=https://www.thetimes.com/travel/inspiration/ski-holiday/anton-freud-0928lb952dg|url-access=subscription}}</ref>  Walter Freud and his wife are buried in the [[Freud Corner (Golders Green Crematorium)|"Freud Corner"]] at [[Golders Green Crematorium]], London.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://static-secure.guim.co.uk/sys-images/Guardian/About/General/2014/1/15/1389794713994/Urn-containing-Sigmund-Fr-014.jpg |title=Photograph of Urn containing Sigmund Freud |work=The Guardian |year=2014 |access-date=16 October 2014}}</ref>

In 2022  [[Der Spiegel|Spiegel TV]] produced a docu-drama based on Freud's work with the War Crimes Investigation Unit: ''Nazijäger – Reise in die Finsternis''.<ref>{{Cite web | last = Kloft | first = Michael | title = Wie der Enkel von Sigmund Freud zum Nazijäger wurde | publisher =Spiegel Geschichte | date =16 January 2022| url = https://www.spiegel.de/geschichte/anton-walter-freud-wie-der-enkel-von-sigmund-freud-zum-nazijaeger-wurde-a-bfc514b0-ee86-426a-b9d4-0de56dbaa01d |access-date =3 October 2022}}</ref>
